skill.name: skywork-document
skill.description: Create formatted documents through the Skywork Office Doc API from prompts and reference files. It can parse source files, request cloud document generation, and download finished DOCX, PDF, HTML, or Markdown outputs.
skill.summary: Generate structured Skywork documents from prompts and reference files.
skill.author: SkyworkAI

security_audit.summary: The skill is a cloud document generator with real network, file upload, credential storage, and browser-login behavior. I confirmed the substantive risks around external processing, token caching, endpoint overrides, and Windows shell use, while marking Markdown backtick detections as false positives. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: User prompts and reference files are sent to Skywork cloud APIs.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear user consent before upload and document which data types are sent to Skywork services.

remediation.issue: Skywork tokens are cached in ~/.skywork_token without permission hardening.
remediation.suggestion: Use a platform credential store or create the token file with owner-only permissions such as 0600.

remediation.issue: The Windows login flow uses subprocess.Popen with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True browser launch with webbrowser.open, os.startfile, or a fixed argument call without shell interpretation.

remediation.issue: Environment variables can redirect Skywork API and login endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Validate endpoint hosts against an allowlist before sending files, prompts, or tokens.

remediation.issue: Parsed content can be written to a caller-selected output path.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting files and prefer writing outputs inside the current workspace or a dedicated output directory.

semantic_findings.title: External Processing of User Files and Prompts
semantic_findings.description: The skill reads local reference files, uploads them to Skywork, and sends document prompts to Skywork APIs. This is expected functionality, but users must understand that their content leaves the local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly reads file bytes, posts them to a remote API, and sends document content in the request payload. The behavior is central to the skill and clearly evidenced.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Cache Lacks Permission Hardening
semantic_findings.description: The authentication module saves Skywork token data to ~/.skywork_token using a normal file write. No chmod, secure file creation, or platform credential store is used around the token cache.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token cache path and write operation are explicit, and there is no nearby permission hardening. This makes the credential storage concern high confidence.

semantic_findings.title: Environment-Controlled Endpoints Can Redirect Sensitive Data
semantic_findings.description: Several API base URLs can be overridden by environment variables before files, prompts, or token checks are sent. This is useful for configuration but risky in shared or compromised environments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint overrides are explicit and are used by network calls that process sensitive data. The risk depends on environment trust, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Long document requests often need structure, reference files, and formatted delivery. This skill uses Skywork document services to create polished files from prompts and uploaded materials.
actual_capabilities: Authenticates with Skywork using an environment token, cached token, or browser login.
Uploads a reference file to Skywork for server-side parsing and returns a reusable file ID.
Creates documents from a title, detailed content prompt, language, format, and optional parsed file IDs.
Streams document generation progress from the Skywork API through server-sent events.
Downloads generated document files to the current working directory when a file URL is returned.
Supports DOCX, PDF, HTML, and Markdown output formats.
limitations: Requires a Skywork account, network access, and a valid Skywork token.
Uploads prompts and reference files to Skywork cloud services for processing.
Generation can take several minutes for complex documents.
The skill does not edit existing documents locally without using the Skywork API.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Reports
use_cases.description: Create structured reports from a prompt and supporting PDFs, spreadsheets, or notes.

use_cases.title: Convert Research Into Documents
use_cases.description: Turn gathered research and source files into a formatted DOCX, PDF, HTML, or Markdown document.

use_cases.title: Draft Business Materials
use_cases.description: Generate polished plans, briefs, summaries, and proposals in the requested language and format.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-page DOCX overview about renewable energy trends in English with clear headings and a concise conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Use One Reference File
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using one uploaded source.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the attached PDF as the source and create a client-ready PDF summary with key findings, risks, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Multiple Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with several parsed files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a market analysis report from the attached files. Compare sources, highlight conflicts, and include an executive summary.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Multilingual Formal Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with format, language, and structure constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a formal Markdown report in Spanish using the uploaded research. Include methodology, findings, recommendations, and appendix notes.

output_examples.input: User asks for a DOCX proposal based on a short business brief.
output_examples.output: A downloadable DOCX proposal with sections for goals, scope, timeline, pricing notes, and recommended next steps.

output_examples.input: User provides a PDF research paper and asks for a summary report.
output_examples.output: A PDF report with an executive summary, major findings, evidence notes, limitations, and a local saved file path.

output_examples.input: User asks for a Markdown project plan in German from several source files.
output_examples.output: A Markdown document with milestones, responsibilities, risks, assumptions, and references derived from the uploaded materials.

best_practices: State the desired format, language, audience, and document structure before generation starts.
Review files for sensitive information before uploading them to Skywork cloud services.
Use clear titles without spaces when passing titles to the document creation script.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for short answers that do not need a generated file.
Do not upload confidential files unless the user accepts external processing by Skywork.
Do not pass vague prompts when the document needs a specific structure or tone.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Skywork account?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs a valid Skywork token from the environment, token cache, or browser login flow.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The scripts support DOCX, PDF, HTML, and Markdown output formats.

faq.question: Can it use uploaded files as sources?
faq.answer: Yes. It can parse files through Skywork and pass the returned file IDs into document generation.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: Generated files are downloaded to the current working directory when a file URL is available.

faq.question: Does it send data to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts, uploaded files, and document requests are processed by Skywork cloud APIs.

faq.question: Can it create documents in languages other than English?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts a language option, including English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, and Spanish.
